description: Acute physiological stress / arousal, inferred from wearable signals (heart rate, HRV, electrodermal activity). ML-based module (brief 2) — no clean governing equation. This Layer 1 file supplies (a) population norms used to bootstrap synthetic training data before the real wearable dataset is available, and (b) cited effect sizes for cross-system edges. Target dataset: PhysioNet 'Wearable Exam Stress Dataset' (HR/EDA/HRV, open/credentialed, ~days to access).

rmssd_mean.unit: ms (HRV, root mean square of successive differences)
rmssd_mean.notes: Higher RMSSD = more parasympathetic (recovered) tone; drops under stress.

stress_index_mean.citation: Composite target normalized to 0-100 (operational definition; calibrate on labelled data)
stress_index_mean.notes: Module output. Operational until validated against a LABELLED stress dataset (this exam dataset has no labels).

exam_hr_reference.unit: bpm (mean heart rate under real exam stress)
exam_hr_reference.citation: PhysioNet Wearable Exam Stress Dataset (Empatica E4, 597 5-min windows, fitted)
exam_hr_reference.notes: Real high-stress HR reference; anchors the upper end of the arousal index (resting rest_hr_mean=68 anchors 0). HR elevation is the one cross-person-reliable signal here; wrist EDA/RMSSD absolute values are device-uncalibrated in this dataset.

efficiency_per_stress_point.unit: sleep-efficiency percentage points per stress-index point at bedtime
efficiency_per_stress_point.citation: Kalmbach 2018, J Sleep Res (pre-sleep arousal/stress reduces sleep continuity)
efficiency_per_stress_point.notes: GRADED MODERATE evidence. Build the edge only with a clearly stated confidence; direction well established, exact dose-response less so.
